card.summary: 10 published shows (>15 min) + 10 published tracks (<=15 min). But: 'there's currently no limit to the number of uploads you can have in your drafts'. Drafts...

free_tier.stated: 10 published shows (>15 min) + 10 published tracks (<=15 min). But: 'there's currently no limit to the number of uploads you can have in your drafts'. Drafts are uploaded, stored, and private. That is the actual finding: published storage is capped at 20 items, unpublished storage is uncapped.

egress.terms: Free streaming for listeners; no egress charge to the creator, but drafts are not publicly downloadable at all, so 'egress' is the wrong axis. A draft has no delivery surface.

record.tooling: No public API. Desktop-only upload for tracks ('only available through the desktop platform and not the Mixcloud app'); shows upload from web. No rclone backend, no client library found.
record.chaining: Unlimited drafts x 4 GB per show x N free accounts. Whether drafts are garbage-collected is not stated. The FAQ only says previous uploads are not deleted when you exceed the publish cap, which is a different promise from 'drafts are kept forever'.
record.limits_note: 4 GB max per show file; shows must be >15 min, tracks <=15 min (so the 4 GB ceiling only applies to long files); 10 published shows + 10 published tracks; RSS-fed podcasts also count toward the 10-show cap ('only the 10 most recent shows will display').
record.reliability_note: Mixcloud is a streaming platform: shows are transcoded for playback and there is no original-file download link on Basic. Drafts are inaccessible to anyone but the uploader, which means they are storage but not retrieval. A draft is only recoverable by publishing it, and publishing consumes one of the 10 slots.

evidence.proved: 'Creators on the basic tier can have a total of 10 published shows (over 15 minutes long), and 10 published tracks'; 'we won't delete your previous uploads, and there's currently no limit to the number of uploads you can have in your drafts'
'Choose a file over 15 minutes in length (max 4GB)'; 'Lossless and lossy formats are supported ... WAV, AIFF, FLAC or AAC, OGG, M4A, MP2, MP3 and WMA'
